verses.verse:
दूरवर्ति स्वरस्थानाम् भावानामनु भुतये।
पंचमस्तु सहायः स्यादभावे मध्यमः स्वरः।११६।
verses.text: For the feelings of notes placed far away to be experienced, Pañcama is the helper; in its absence, the note Madhyama.

commentary.text: When we want to do svara-vistāra (elaboration of notes) or ālāpa in a rāga, it is first of all necessary for us to know the separate importance of the notes used in that rāga. Generally the importance of Sa is the same in all rāgas. It will be quite fitting if we regard it as the Mahārājā of the kingdom that is the rāga. After it, the second place has to be given to Pañcama, because it is Sa's helper, in the role of Prime Minister. If Pañcama is varjit (omitted) in that rāga, then in its absence Madhyama is accepted. After that, the vādī (principal note) and saṃvādī (consonant second note) of that rāga we can liken to the Governor and the Chief Minister. Then we give the other notes the place of ordinary subjects. Once such an arrangement is made, moving on the ordinary notes and stopping on the special notes: these are the only two actions we have to do. In moving, the use of tāna elements, and in stopping, a beautiful kampan (shake), will be graceful. In the ālāpa of a rāga my attitude will be that of a curious tourist in a particular city. That is, fixing one place for the night's stay, setting out each day for one important place, and coming back again to the fixed place. If on the way one has to stop a little for some special reason, one must stop only for a short time and keep one's destination in mind. At the destination, walking around and sitting in due manner will come naturally. If some things are left unseen at that place, one can set out for the same place again the next day too. So it is proved that pauses can be made in many ways.
